key.name: window-rules
key.summary: Which decorations are ours, per window kind
key.description: Window kinds this extension decorates, and which decoration axes are ours for each. Keyed by a window-kind fingerprint: '<identity>:client_type=<wayland|x11>,window_type=<int>,has_parent=<bool>,allows_resize=<bool>,attached_dialog=<bool>' e.g. 'wechat:client_type=wayland,window_type=0,has_parent=true,allows_resize=false,attached_dialog=false' The fingerprint is derived from the picked window's stable structural attributes, so a rule never generalizes to every window of an application. The state names the axes that are ours: 'both' (we round the corners and draw the shadow), 'none' (we draw neither; the window stays exactly as the client drew it), 'corners' (we round the corners; the client's own shadow stays untouched), or 'shadow' (we take the shadow over; the client's own corners stay). Structural disqualifiers (non-decorable window type, maximized/fullscreen) are never affected. Rules stored under the previous 'suppress-rules' / 'force-rules' keys are not migrated: the group-plus-axis form has no equivalent here.

key.name: prefer-crisp-text
key.description: Skip rounded corners on fractional scale monitors (retaining shadow) to avoid text blur and resampling overhead.

key.name: resize-band
key.summary: Widen the resize band around windows
key.description: Let windows whose own resize border is narrower than a native one be resized by dragging the band around them: 12 pixels along the sides and 24 at the corners, as native GNOME windows can. A window whose declared margin is already at least 12 pixels on every side is left alone. When off, clicks in that band go to whatever is behind the window
